text:
Noah: quick update from the early-exit + hybrid-reranker bring-up on orion-13b (gptq4)
Aisha: curious  what was the hypothesis for early-exit here?
Noah: reduce p50/p95 token latency by allowing the main path to accept early with a cheap reranker validating critical tokens. idea: speculative prefetch up to 24 tokens, early-exit when reranker confidence > 0.8 and no entity tokens in the last window.
Vikram: what metrics did you collect?
Noah: stratified 4.5k eval: short/mid/long. collected p50/p95 token latency, micro-ROUGE-L (longform), EM (trivia), kv_warmup_hits, rerank_accept_rate, top1_prob_drop on revert, per-token entropy, and per-session cost-estimate ($/session).
Lea: headline numbers?
Noah: p50 token latency baseline 132ms -> early-exit 92ms (30% win). p95 improved 18%. longform ROUGE delta -0.9, trivia EM -1.6. rerank_accept_rate 64%. revert_rate when reranker failed ~0.11 per session. cost per session down ~16%.
Aisha: ROUGE drop seems non-trivial. where did it manifest?
Noah: concentrated in mid-long multi-step instructs (200-700 tokens) where the model accepted an early token that collapsed a later sub-step. many cases are "missing explicit command" errors rather than hallucinations.
Vikram: did reranker use full context or a compressed prefix?
Noah: cheap reranker is convolutional BERT-lite over last 64 tokens + rescoring logits for next-token validity. we kept it intentionally lightweight to avoid CPU blowup.
Lea: did you try stronger rerankers or raising confidence threshold?
Noah: yes small sweep: threshold 0.8 -> 0.88 recovered ~0.6% ROUGE but accept_rate dropped to 52% and p50 latency increased ~9ms. stronger reranker (distil-bert) recovered another 0.3% ROUGE but added ~6ms on avg and raised CPU cost ~22%.
Aisha: any quant interaction?
Noah: ran int8 arm too. int8 baseline closed ~1.2% EM vs gptq4 baseline; int8+early-exit behaved similarly pattern-wise but errors shifted: int8 had slightly higher top1_prob noise making reranker accept less often (accept_rate -4%). unit cost higher due to slower kernels.
Vikram: KV cache warmups? anything there?
Noah: early-exit sessions showed ~7% fewer kv_warmup_hits on mid contexts, correlating with the missing-step errors. hypothesis: prefetch window sometimes fetched stale KV slices if early accepted tokens changed alignment.
Lea: interesting. are there routing rules to mitigate?
Noah: prototype conditional policy: if prompt_len>220 OR ner_density>0.08 -> disable early-exit (route to conservative lane); else allow early-exit. Pilot routing reduced ROUGE delta to -0.4 while preserving ~18% latency win across traffic.
Aisha: rollout guardrails?
Noah: plan: 3-stage canary. 1) staging 10k holdout with conditional routing + int8 arm (run queued). 2) blind human eval top 300 diffs. 3) 1% prod canary with autopilot rollback if cohort ROUGE drop >0.8 or trivia EM drop >1.0 or p95 latency regresses >2x.
Vikram: config snippet?
Noah: paste: `{"early_exit":true,"reranker":"bert-lite","accept_conf":0.8,"prefetch":24,"entity_gate":true,"entity_threshold":0.08}`
Lea: nice. any idea on cost tradeoffs for product?
Noah: rough numbers: conservative lane cost per session ~+$0.03 vs aggressive early-exit saves ~$0.05/session on GPU time. net depends on fraction routed to conservative. Redwood Optimize asked to compute pareto curve (latency vs ROUGE vs $/session) for us.
Aisha: human eval plan? who will run it?
Noah: Lea + two contract raters. blind A/B on 300 disagreements, accept if human preference for baseline over early-exit <20% OR if disagreements are mostly stylistic.
ci-bot: queued job "early-exit-orion-stratified-2026-03-22" -> staging (job id: 11031)
Vikram: anything else we should instrument?
Noah: add per-token alignment delta (position shift after accept) and prefix-entity-change flag. those helped debug the KV alignment issue in a follow-up.
Lea: sounds good. once staging run completes, drop diffs in /mnt/holdouts/early_exit_orion_2026 and ping for human eval.
Aisha: thanks Noah. schedule looks reasonable. :thumbsup:
